digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III; Pakia (2005) App. VI; Maundu & Tengnäs 2005 (Mchimwemwe)

teaser.en: Its name means 'smile', and it is used as a charm to win the warmth and goodwill of friends and workmates.

summary.en: *Chimwemwe* is the bushveld gardenia, a twiggy tree with large, fragrant white trumpet flowers. It gives cooking sticks and medicine, and is used magically to win smiles and appreciation.

about.en:
*Chimwemwe* is a twiggy, stiff-branched tree up to about 8 m. Its spoon-shaped leaves grow in whorls of three at the tips of short shoots. The flowers are large white trumpets that fade to yellow and smell sweet, especially in the evening.

The fruits are hard, oval and ribbed, and can stay on the tree for a long time.

where.en: It grows in bushland and wooded grassland. It is easiest to find when the white, fragrant flowers are open.

uses.en: The hard wood is shaped into cooking stirrers and sticks. The plant is also used in traditional medicine and in ceremonies.

culture.en: The name *chimwemwe* means 'smile'. The plant is used magically to win appreciation and smiles from peers and workmates, a charm for goodwill as pleasant as its flowers.

names.en: Pakia records the Digo name *chimwemwe*; ICRAF's handbook gives *mchimwemwe*. In Swahili and Giriama it is *mkimwemwe*. In English it is the bushveld gardenia.

reason.en: Another shrub used as a charm for status

sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: an ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD thesis, Univ. Bayreuth, Appendix III (Digo–botanical name list) & Appendix VI (name semantics). https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
